title: In vivo gain-of-function cDNA library screening for colonization genes in a mouse model of pulmonary metastasis
protocol: Measure 25 g of LB broth powder and 15 g of bacteriological agar in 1 L ultrapure water.
Swirl to mix the components in the ultrapure water.
Autoclave the mixture on liquid cycle (121°C, 30 min).
Cool the autoclaved mixture to around 50°C in a temperature-controlled water bath.
Add Ampicillin to achieve a final concentration of 100 μg/mL.
Pour the mixture into 18–20 15 cm plates (15–20 mL per plate) and allow it to solidify at room temperature (25°C).
Dilute 1 μL of the bacterial plasmid library into 1 mL of LB broth and mix by gentle vortexing as Dilution A.
Dilute 1 μL of Dilution A into 1 mL of LB broth and mix by gentle vortexing as Dilution B.
Remove 50 μL aliquots from Dilution B and spread onto each prewarmed LB/Amp agar plate.
Leave the plates at room temperature (25°C) for 20 min.
Incubate the plates inverted at 37°C overnight.
Count the total number of colonies on the plates.
Calculate the titer using the formula: (colony# from Dilution B/Plating volume) × 10^6 = colony-forming unit (cfu) per mL.
Prepare 1 μL of 1,000-fold-diluted cDNA library culture in E.coli DH10B.
Dilute the cDNA library culture in 150 μL of LB broth.
Spread the diluted culture on 20 plates (150-mm).
Incubate plates at 37°C overnight.
Add 5 mL of LB medium to each plate.
Scrape off colonies into 2 liters of LB/Amp broth.
Incubate cultures in a shaking incubator at 37°C until the OD600 > 2.0.
Proceed with plasmid isolation using QIAGEN Maxi Prep.
Use the 5′ and 3′ LIB primers to amplify cDNA inserts by Advantage™-GC 2 PCR Kit.
Amplify cDNA inserts in a C1000 Thermal Cycler for verification of cDNA representation.
Conduct gel electrophoresis on the reactions to see a smear pattern consistent with the library size intervals.
Mix flanking linkers compatible with 5′ and 3′ LIB primers to the 5′ and 3′ insert ends of cDNA libraries if preparing in-house.
Store amplified bacterial library frozen in 33% glycerol at -80°C for later use if necessary.
Plate HEK293T cells at a density of 6.0 × 10^6 cells per 100-mm plate 12 hours before transfection.
Replace old medium with fresh medium before transfection (1–2 h).
Transfect 10 μg of plasmid DNA along with 1 μg pCMV-VSV and 10 μg pUMVC using 63 μL Lipofectamine 2000 per 100-mm plate.
Gently swirl plates to ensure the transfection solution is uniformly distributed.
Aspirate old medium at 10–12 h post-transfection.
Wash cells twice with 1× PBS.
Add 5–6 mL of fresh medium.
Aspirate medium 32–38 h after transfection.
Pass through 0.45 μm filters.
Store media containing undiluted viral particles at 4°C for use within 24 h or freeze at -80°C for later use.
Infect DU145 cells with pRRL3 lentivirus to generate GFP-DU145 cells.
Plate GFP-DU145 cells at a density of 2.0 × 10^6 cells per 100-mm plate 12 h before infection.
Generate a 1:10 dilution of the filtered library virus.
Administer the diluted virus to GFP-DU145 cells in the presence of 5 μg/mL polybrene for 18 hours.
Conduct genomic PCR of infected cells after 48–72 hours using 5′ and 3′ LIB primers.
Dilute the virus-containing media at least two-fold with fresh media before administration.
Maintain a multiplicity of infection (MOI) that is substantially lower than the number of cells to be infected.
Use an MOI of 0.2 as determined by alkaline phosphatase activity in infected cells for surrogate measure of viral titer and virion numbers.
Assess percentage of cells transduced using pLAPSN expression plasmid.
Combine dilution factor, number of cells plated with the percentage of cells transduced to calculate viral titer and virion numbers.
Mix 1.5 × 10^5 infected GFP-DU145 cells in 100 μL PBS supplemented with 1% FBS.
Intravenously inject the cell suspension via tail vein into recipient NOD/SCID mice (8-10 weeks old).
After 18 days, sacrifice the mice.
Excise and wash lungs in ice cold PBS.
Lay down extracted lungs flat on a clean TC plate.
Examine metastatic colonies using fluorescence-equipped dissecting SteREO stereomicroscope.
Surgically cut pieces of lungs harboring distinct visible GFP-positive colonies (∼1 mm in diameter).
Minimize carryover of peripheral lung tissues.
Isolate genomic DNA from GFP-positive colonies using Qiagen DNeasy.
Amplify DNA using manufacturer-supplied 5′ and 3′ linker primers following PicoMaxx High Fidelity PCR system guidelines.
Resolve amplification reactions using 1% agarose electrophoresis.
Cut out resolved sequences.
Send out cut-out sequences for DNA sequencing.
BLAST the sequenced genes for identification.
